record.paper_title: Billiard dynamics: A survey with the emphasis on open problems
record.original_question: If the limit h = lim_{n→∞} (log f_Y(n))/n exists for a dispersing billiard table Y, is h equal to the topological entropy of the billiard map?

evidence.quote: Задача 6. Если предел в уравнении (2.2) действительно существует, является ли h топологической энтропией биллиардного отображения?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Y$ be a dispersing (Sinai) billiard table: a compact domain in the plane (or on the 2-torus) whose boundary consists of finitely many smooth strictly convex arcs (curved away from the interior), possibly with corners. The billiard flow is generated by the free motion of a point particle inside $Y$ with elastic reflections at the boundary, and the billiard map $T$ acts on the cross-section $M$ consisting of unit tangent vectors based at the boundary and pointing inward.

For each integer $n \geq 1$, let $f_Y(n)$ denote the number of periodic orbits of the billiard map $T$ of period at most $n$ (equivalently, the number of periodic billiard trajectories in $Y$ making at most $n$ reflections). Suppose that the limit
$$h \;=\; \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{\log f_Y(n)}{n}$$
exists and is finite.

Question: Must $h$ equal the topological entropy $h_{\mathrm{top}}(T)$ of the billiard map $T$?
artifact.status_search_result: For non-degenerate semi-dispersing billiards, finiteness of topological entropy and at-most-exponential growth of periodic orbits are known (Burago–Ferleger and related work), but the equality of the exponential growth rate of periodic orbits with the topological entropy in the dispersing case is not established as a theorem in the literature found, and is repeatedly listed as an open question in surveys on billiard dynamics.

status_evidence.title: Topological Entropy Of Semi-Dispersing Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Burago–Ferleger style estimates give finiteness of topological entropy and at-most-exponential growth of periodic trajectories for non-degenerate semi-dispersing billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Upper bounds on periodic orbit growth and finiteness of entropy are known, but equality with the exponential orbit growth rate is not asserted.

status_evidence.title: Topological Entropy and Pressure for Finite Horizon Sinai Billiards (Demers, ICM)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of variational principle and equilibrium states for Sinai billiards; matching of orbit growth rate with topological entropy is discussed as part of ongoing program.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys treat the relation between counting periodic orbits and topological entropy in dispersing billiards as part of an active research program.
